question: What is the main goal of a surgical hand scrub compared to a normal quick wash?

options.A: To greatly reduce germ numbers and stop them from multiplying
options.B: To completely get rid of all germs on the skin
options.C: To wash away visible dirt with plain soap
options.D: To permanently kill all sweat glands

explanation: You've got this! Germs live deep in our skin and can never be completely wiped out, so our goal is to lower their numbers and keep them from growing. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Why is it impossible to make human skin completely germ-free during a surgical scrub?

options.A: Soap cannot touch the outer layer of skin
options.B: Scrubs are only meant to wash away dirt
options.C: The sink water is never hot enough to kill germs
options.D: Germs hide deep inside hair roots and oil glands

explanation: Think of it like tiny hiding spots! Microbes live deep down in skin structures like hair follicles, making total sterilization impossible. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h1)

question: Which item is completely banned for nurses to wear on their hands and wrists before a scrub?

options.B: All jewelry including rings and watches

explanation: Ring and watch bands trap moisture and hide loads of bacteria underneath, so off they all must come! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: A nurse is getting ready for surgery and notices a fresh scratch on the back of her hand. What should she do?

options.A: Rub antiseptic over it and wear double gloves
options.B: Report the scratch and take on a non-sterile role
options.C: Scrub for a longer time using special soap
options.D: Cover it tightly with a waterproof plaster and go ahead

explanation: Safety first! Open cuts let bacteria escape into the sterile field, so it's best to step back and take a non-sterile duty. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h2)

question: What makes chlorhexidine gluconate a popular antiseptic choice in the theatre?

options.A: It works instantly with zero contact time
options.B: It kills viruses faster than any other chemical
options.C: It is easily washed away by hard water
options.D: It keeps fighting bacteria and prevents growth for hours

explanation: Chlorhexidine is great because it binds to your skin and keeps working long after you've finished scrubbing! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which antiseptic needs to dry on the skin so it can slowly release free iodine to kill germs?
explanation: Povidone-iodine needs a little drying time to work its magic and release free iodine onto your skin. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h3)

question: During a surgical scrub, why must you keep your hands higher than your elbows at all times?

options.A: To easily reach the wall soap dispenser
options.C: To let more oxygen flow into your arm muscles
options.D: To stop dirty water and soap from running back down onto your clean hands

explanation: Gravity is always pulling down! Keeping hands high ensures dirty water runs away from your clean fingers. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: When scrubbing and rinsing your arms, which direction should you always go?

options.A: Beginning at your upper arm and moving down
options.B: From your elbows down toward your fingertips
options.C: Starting at your wrists and moving in circles
options.D: From your fingertips up toward your elbows

explanation: Always move from the cleanest part (fingertips) to the less clean part (elbows). Easy to remember! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h4)

question: You just finished your scrub and need to dry your hands with a sterile towel. What is the correct way to do it?

options.A: Wipe your upper arm first and finish with your fingers
options.B: Use the middle of the towel for both hands at once
options.C: Rub vigorously back and forth all over your arm
options.D: Blot and rotate gently from your fingertips down to your elbow

explanation: Be gentle with your skin! Blot from clean fingers to dirty elbows to avoid irritation and keep things sterile. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: How should a scrubbed nurse enter the operating room after finishing their scrub?

options.A: Back through the door to keep hands safe and away from clothing
options.B: Ask an unscrubbed colleague to open the door and pull them in
options.C: Push the door open while keeping hands high near the face
options.D: Turn sideways and slide through a narrow opening

explanation: Backing in ensures your front and clean hands don't accidentally brush against the door or your scrubs. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h5)

question: Oops! A scrubbed nurse accidentally drops their hands below waist level before putting on a gown. What should they do?

options.A: Ask the circulator to spray antiseptic on the hands
options.B: Lift hands back up and start gowning
options.C: Wipe hands quickly with alcohol rub and keep going
options.D: Treat the hands as contaminated and repeat the entire scrub

explanation: Anything below the waist is considered unsafe territory. Better safe than sorry—time for a quick re-scrub! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)

question: Which of these actions is NOT allowed during a surgical hand scrub?

options.A: Using disposable picks to clean under your fingernails
options.B: Leaning against the sink edge to rest your arms
options.C: Keeping your hands higher than your elbows
options.D: Standing at a safe distance from the sink

explanation: Leaning against the sink transfers germs from your scrubs to your body, breaking sterility and forcing a re-scrub. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T6#GNS123_U5_T6_h6)
